title: Revelation 6 — The seven seals: Four Horsemen + cosmic-signs

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — Codex Sinaiticus (א/01, 4th c. CE ~330-360) as primary uncial witness; NB Codex Vaticanus (B/03) is INCOMPLETE for Revelation. Cross-collation against Codex Alexandrinus (A/02, 5th c. CE — often the SUPERIOR Revelation witness on internal grounds), Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04, 5th c. palimpsest). P47 (Chester Beatty III, ~250 CE) does NOT preserve Rev 6 — P47 begins at Rev 9:10. P115 (P.Oxy 4499) lacunose. P18 preserves Rev 1:4-7 only. SBLGNT base text.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ εἶδον ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὸ ἀρνίον μίαν ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ σφραγίδων, καὶ ἤκουσα ἑνὸς ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγοντος ὡς φωνὴ βροντῆς· Ἔρχου.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eidon hote ēnoixen to arnion mian ek tōn hepta sphragidōn, kai ēkousa henos ek tōn tessarōn zōōn legontos hōs phōnē brontēs· Erchou.

i18n.en: And I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying with a voice like thunder: "Come!"

paragraphs.commentary: Textual variant: NA28/SBLGNT read short *Erchou* 'Come!' (addressed to the horseman); Byzantine majority + TR + KJV read *Erchou kai ide* 'Come and see!' (addressed to John). The variant is a quartet-pattern: the short form is repeated at seals 2, 3, 4. The WoH-Translation preserves the critical-text short form *Erchou*. **MAJOR FOUR-HORSEMEN SITE.** See central-glossary entry `four-horsemen-rev-6-1-8-zechariah-1-6-cross-corpus`. Cross-corpus to Zech 1:8-11 + Zech 6:1-8 horse-and-chariot visions.

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος λευκός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων τόξον, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στέφανος, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν νικῶν καὶ ἵνα νικήσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eidon, kai idou hippos leukos, kai ho kathēmenos ep’ auton echōn toxon, kai edothē autō stephanos, kai exēlthen nikōn kai hina nikēsē.

i18n.en: And I looked, and behold, a white horse, and the one seated on it had a bow, and a crown was given to him, and he went out conquering and to conquer.

paragraphs.commentary: **THE WHITE HORSE — MAJOR INTERPRETIVE CRUX.** Four readings: (a) Christ — Caird 1966 BNTC, the patristic Irenaeus + Athanasius tradition; (b) the Antichrist — Beale NIGTC 376-378, Aune WBC 391-394 (the parody-of-Christ reading); (c) a generic-conquest-and-victory figure — Bauckham 1993 *Climax of Prophecy* (the four-horsemen-as-four-judgments-on-the-world reading); (d) the Parthian-cavalry threat — Koester AB 392-394 (the historical-contextual reading; the Parthian mounted-archers were the eastern-frontier military threat to Rome). The interpretation is contested; the WoH-Translation surface English preserves the conventional rendering. Documented at central-glossary entry `four-horsemen-rev-6-1-8-zechariah-1-6-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν δευτέραν, ἤκουσα τοῦ δευτέρου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hote ēnoixen tēn sphragida tēn deuteran, ēkousa tou deuterou zōou legontos· Erchou.

i18n.en: And when he opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying: "Come!"

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἄλλος ἵππος πυρρός, καὶ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἐδόθη αὐτῷ λαβεῖν τὴν εἰρήνην ἐκ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἵνα ἀλλήλους σφάξουσιν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ μάχαιρα μεγάλη.
paragraphs.translit: kai exēlthen allos hippos pyrros, kai tō kathēmenō ep’ auton edothē autō labein tēn eirēnēn ek tēs gēs kai hina allēlous sphaxousin, kai edothē autō machaira megalē.

i18n.en: And another horse came out, fiery red, and to the one seated on it was given to take peace from the earth, so that people should slay one another, and a great sword was given to him.

paragraphs.commentary: The *hippos pyrros* (fiery-red horse / war). Civil-war imagery (*allēlous sphaxousin* 'they slay one another'); cross-corpus to Zech 1:8 (the red horse of Zechariah's first vision) + Zech 6:2 (the red horses of the first chariot).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τρίτην, ἤκουσα τοῦ τρίτου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου. καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος μέλας, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔχων ζυγὸν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hote ēnoixen tēn sphragida tēn tritēn, ēkousa tou tritou zōou legontos· Erchou. kai eidon, kai idou hippos melas, kai ho kathēmenos ep’ auton echōn zygon en tē cheiri autou.

i18n.en: And when he opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying: "Come!" And I looked, and behold, a black horse, and the one seated on it had a balance in his hand.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἤκουσα ὡς φωνὴν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων λέγουσαν· Χοῖνιξ σίτου δηναρίου, καὶ τρεῖς χοίνικες κριθῶν δηναρίου· καὶ τὸ ἔλαιον καὶ τὸν οἶνον μὴ ἀδικήσῃς.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkousa hōs phōnēn en mesō tōn tessarōn zōōn legousan· Choinix sitou dēnariou, kai treis choinikes krithōn dēnariou· kai to elaion kai ton oinon mē adikēsēs.

i18n.en: And I heard what seemed to be a voice in the midst of the four living creatures saying: "A quart of wheat for a denarius, and three quarts of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the oil and the wine."

paragraphs.commentary: The *hippos melas* (black horse / famine) + the famine-pricing oracle: *choinix sitou dēnariou kai treis choinikes krithōn dēnariou* 'a measure of wheat for a denarius, and three measures of barley for a denarius'. A denarius was approximately a day's wage; a *choinix* approximately a day's-grain-ration. The oracle therefore describes a 10x-to-12x normal-grain-price — famine-conditions but not subsistence-failure (cf. the Domitianic price-fixing edict on grain prices documented in epigraphic and papyrological evidence).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν τετάρτην, ἤκουσα φωνὴν τοῦ τετάρτου ζῴου λέγοντος· Ἔρχου.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hote ēnoixen tēn sphragida tēn tetartēn, ēkousa phōnēn tou tetartou zōou legontos· Erchou.

i18n.en: And when he opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying: "Come!"

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἵππος χλωρός, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ ὄνομα αὐτῷ ὁ Θάνατος, καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἠκολούθει μετ’ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἐξουσία ἐπὶ τὸ τέταρτον τῆς γῆς, ἀποκτεῖναι ἐν ῥομφαίᾳ καὶ ἐν λιμῷ καὶ ἐν θανάτῳ καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν θηρίων τῆς γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai eidon, kai idou hippos chlōros, kai ho kathēmenos epanō autou onoma autō ho Thanatos, kai ho hadēs ēkolouthei met’ autou· kai edothē autois exousia epi to tetarton tēs gēs, apokteinai en rhomphaia kai en limō kai en thanatō kai hypo tōn thēriōn tēs gēs.

i18n.en: And I looked, and behold, a pale green horse, and the one seated on it — his name was Death, and Hades was following with him. And authority was given to them over a quarter of the earth, to kill with sword and with famine and with pestilence and by the wild beasts of the earth.

paragraphs.commentary: The *hippos chlōros* (pale-green horse / Death) + Hades following. **MAJOR PHILOLOGICAL CRUX.** Greek *chlōros* fundamentally means 'green' but extends in Hellenistic-Greek to 'pale' / 'sallow' / 'sickly-green' (Thucydides 2.49 for plague-victim-complexion). The dominant English-translation tradition renders 'pale' on the surface (KJV/RSV/NIV); NRSV renders 'pale green'. The death-association context (the fourth-horseman is named Thanatos / Death followed by Hades) supports the 'sickly-green corpse-color' reading. Documented at overlay-glossary entry `chloros-rev-6-8-pale-green-horse-rendering-convention` and central-glossary entry `four-horsemen-rev-6-1-8-zechariah-1-6-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν πέμπτην σφραγῖδα, εἶδον ὑποκάτω τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐσφαγμένων διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν εἶχον.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hote ēnoixen tēn pemptēn sphragida, eidon hypokatō tou thysiastēriou tas psychas tōn esphagmenōn dia ton logon tou theou kai dia tēn martyrian hēn eichon.

i18n.en: And when he opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slain for the word of God and for the witness that they had borne.

paragraphs.commentary: The fifth seal: martyr-souls under the altar (*hypokatō tou thysiastēriou*). Cross-corpus to the Maccabean-martyr-tradition (2 Macc 7; 4 Macc) and the broader Second-Temple-Jewish martyrology. The 'how-long' (*heōs pote*) cry directly echoes the Hebrew-prophetic-and-psalmic *ʿaḏ-māṯay* lament tradition (Ps 13:1-2; Hab 1:2; Zech 1:12).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔκραξαν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγοντες· Ἕως πότε, ὁ δεσπότης ὁ ἅγιος καὶ ἀληθινός, οὐ κρίνεις καὶ ἐκδικεῖς τὸ αἷμα ἡμῶν ἐκ τῶν κατοικούντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;
paragraphs.translit: kai ekraxan phōnē megalē legontes· Heōs pote, ho despotēs ho hagios kai alēthinos, ou krineis kai ekdikeis to haima hēmōn ek tōn katoikountōn epi tēs gēs?

i18n.en: And they cried out with a loud voice, saying: "How long, O Sovereign Lord, holy and true, until you judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?"

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἑκάστῳ στολὴ λευκή, καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα ἀναπαύσωνται ἔτι χρόνον μικρόν, ἕως πληρωθῶσιν καὶ οἱ σύνδουλοι αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτῶν οἱ μέλλοντες ἀποκτέννεσθαι ὡς καὶ αὐτοί.
paragraphs.translit: kai edothē autois hekastō stolē leukē, kai errethē autois hina anapausōntai eti chronon mikron, heōs plērōthōsin kai hoi syndouloi autōn kai hoi adelphoi autōn hoi mellontes apoktennesthai hōs kai autoi.

i18n.en: And a white robe was given to each of them, and they were told to rest a little longer, until the number of their fellow servants and their brothers should be complete, who were to be killed as they themselves had been.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ εἶδον ὅτε ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν ἕκτην, καὶ σεισμὸς μέγας ἐγένετο, καὶ ὁ ἥλιος ἐγένετο μέλας ὡς σάκκος τρίχινος, καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὅλη ἐγένετο ὡς αἷμα,
paragraphs.translit: Kai eidon hote ēnoixen tēn sphragida tēn hektēn, kai seismos megas egeneto, kai ho hēlios egeneto melas hōs sakkos trichinos, kai hē selēnē holē egeneto hōs haima,

i18n.en: And I saw when he opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake, and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the whole moon became like blood,

paragraphs.commentary: **MAJOR COSMIC-SIGNS SITE.** Sixth-seal cosmic-signs: *seismos megas* (great earthquake) + *hēlios egeneto melas hōs sakkos trichinos* (the sun became black as sackcloth of hair) + *hē selēnē holē egeneto hōs haima* (the whole moon became as blood) + *hoi asteres tou ouranou epesan eis tēn gēn* (the stars of heaven fell to the earth). Cross-corpus chain: Joel 2:30-31 → Isa 13:10 + Isa 34:4 → Mk 13:24-25 → Lk 21:25-26 → Acts 2:19-20 → Rev 6:12-13. The most-systematic NT integration of multiple HB cosmic-signs passages. Documented at central-glossary entry `cosmic-signs-cluster-joel-2-mark-13-acts-2-luke-21-rev-6-cross-corpus`. Bidirectional cross-corpus with v2.60.0 Qur'an `inshiqaq-al-qamar-splitting-of-the-moon-sura-54-1`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἔπεσαν εἰς τὴν γῆν, ὡς συκῆ βάλλει τοὺς ὀλύνθους αὐτῆς ὑπὸ ἀνέμου μεγάλου σειομένη,
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi asteres tou ouranou epesan eis tēn gēn, hōs sykē ballei tous olynthous autēs hypo anemou megalou seiomenē,

i18n.en: and the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree casts its unripe figs when shaken by a great wind,

paragraphs.commentary: *hoi asteres tou ouranou epesan eis tēn gēn* (the stars of heaven fell to the earth). The stars-falling imagery directly echoes Isa 34:4 (*nāmaqqû kol-ṣĕḇāʾ ha-šāmayim* 'all the host of heaven shall rot away'). The *hōs sykē balei tous olynthous autēs* fig-tree-shedding-unripe-fruit simile is a Revelation-distinctive imagery.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὁ οὐρανὸς ἀπεχωρίσθη ὡς βιβλίον ἑλισσόμενον, καὶ πᾶν ὄρος καὶ νῆσος ἐκ τῶν τόπων αὐτῶν ἐκινήθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho ouranos apechōristhē hōs biblion helissomenon, kai pan oros kai nēsos ek tōn topōn autōn ekinēthēsan.

i18n.en: and the heaven was split apart like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place.

paragraphs.commentary: *ho ouranos apechōristhē hōs biblion helissomenon* 'the heaven was rolled up like a scroll' — directly citing Isa 34:4 LXX *kai helichthēsetai ho ouranos hōs biblion*. The systematic-citation pattern is one of the most-pervasive features of the Apocalypse: virtually-every-image draws on the HB prophetic-apocalyptic corpus, often verbatim.

paragraphs.text: καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ οἱ μεγιστᾶνες καὶ οἱ χιλίαρχοι καὶ οἱ πλούσιοι καὶ οἱ ἰσχυροὶ καὶ πᾶς δοῦλος καὶ ἐλεύθερος ἔκρυψαν ἑαυτοὺς εἰς τὰ σπήλαια καὶ εἰς τὰς πέτρας τῶν ὀρέων·
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi basileis tēs gēs kai hoi megistanes kai hoi chiliarchoi kai hoi plousioi kai hoi ischyroi kai pas doulos kai eleutheros ekrypsan heautous eis ta spēlaia kai eis tas petras tōn oreōn·

i18n.en: And the kings of the earth and the magnates and the military commanders and the rich and the strong and every slave and free hid themselves in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains;

paragraphs.text: καὶ λέγουσιν τοῖς ὄρεσιν καὶ ταῖς πέτραις· Πέσετε ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς καὶ κρύψατε ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀργῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου,
paragraphs.translit: kai legousin tois oresin kai tais petrais· Pesete eph’ hēmas kai krypsate hēmas apo prosōpou tou kathēmenou epi tou thronou kai apo tēs orgēs tou arniou,

i18n.en: and they say to the mountains and to the rocks: "Fall on us, and hide us from the face of the one seated on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb,

paragraphs.commentary: Wrath-of-the-Lamb response: the seven-fold social-hierarchy hiding in caves and rocks. *kryptesthe hēmas apo prosōpou tou kathēmenou epi tou thronou kai apo tēs orgēs tou arniou* 'hide us from the face of the One seated on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb' — the social-hierarchy listing (kings + great-men + chiliarchs + rich-men + strong-men + slaves + free-men) reactivates the Isa 2:10, 19, 21 hiding-from-the-terror-of-YHWH tradition.

paragraphs.text: ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ἡμέρα ἡ μεγάλη τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτῶν, καὶ τίς δύναται σταθῆναι;
paragraphs.translit: hoti ēlthen hē hēmera hē megalē tēs orgēs autōn, kai tis dynatai stathēnai?

i18n.en: for the great day of their wrath has come, and who is able to stand?"
